Steampipe: select * from cloud;

Dynamically query APIs, code and more with SQL.
Zero-ETL from 140+ data sources.
	
Common commands:
	
  # Interactive SQL query console
  steampipe query
	
  # Install a plugin from the hub - https://hub.steampipe.io
  steampipe plugin install aws

  # Execute a defined SQL query
  steampipe query "select * from aws_s3_bucket"

  # Get help for a command
  steampipe help query
	
Documentation: https://steampipe.io/docs

Usage:
  steampipe [command]

Available Commands:
  completion     Generate completion scripts
  help           Help about any command
  login          Login to Turbot Pipes
  plugin         Steampipe plugin management
  query          Execute SQL queries interactively or by argument
  service        Steampipe service management

Flags:
  -h, --help                 Help for steampipe
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
  -v, --version              version for steampipe
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Use "steampipe [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Steampipe plugin management.

Plugins extend Steampipe to work with many different services and providers.
Find plugins using the public registry at https://hub.steampipe.io.

Examples:

  # Install a plugin
  steampipe plugin install aws

  # Update a plugin
  steampipe plugin update aws

  # List installed plugins
  steampipe plugin list

  # Uninstall a plugin
  steampipe plugin uninstall aws

Usage:
  steampipe plugin [command]

Available Commands:
  install     Install one or more plugins
  list        List currently installed plugins
  uninstall   Uninstall a plugin
  update      Update one or more plugins

Flags:
  -h, --help   Help for plugin

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Use "steampipe plugin [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Install one or more plugins.

Install a Steampipe plugin, making it available for queries and configuration.
The plugin name format is [registry/org/]name[@version]. The default
registry is hub.steampipe.io, default org is turbot and default version
is latest. The name is a required argument.

Examples:

  # Install all missing plugins that are specified in configuration files
  steampipe plugin install

  # Install a common plugin (turbot/aws)
  steampipe plugin install aws

  # Install a specific plugin version
  steampipe plugin install turbot/azure@0.1.0

  # Hide progress bars during installation
  steampipe plugin install --progress=false aws

  # Skip creation of default plugin config file
  steampipe plugin install --skip-config aws

Usage:
  steampipe plugin install [flags] [registry/org/]name[@version]

Flags:
  -h, --help          Help for plugin install
      --progress      Display installation progress (default true)
      --skip-config   Skip creating the default config file for plugin

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

List currently installed plugins.

List all Steampipe plugins installed for this user.

Examples:

  # List installed plugins
  steampipe plugin list

  # List plugins that have updates available
  steampipe plugin list --outdated

  # List plugins output in json
  steampipe plugin list --output json

Usage:
  steampipe plugin list [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help            Help for plugin list
      --outdated        Check each plugin in the list for updates
      --output string   Output format: table or json (default "table")

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Uninstall a plugin.

Uninstall a Steampipe plugin, removing it from use. The plugin name format is
[registry/org/]name. (Version is not relevant in uninstall, since only one
version of a plugin can be installed at a time.)

Example:

  # Uninstall a common plugin (turbot/aws)
  steampipe plugin uninstall aws

Usage:
  steampipe plugin uninstall [flags] [registry/org/]name

Flags:
  -h, --help   Help for plugin uninstall

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Update plugins.

Update one or more Steampipe plugins, making it available for queries and configuration.
The plugin name format is [registry/org/]name[@version]. The default
registry is hub.steampipe.io, default org is turbot and default version
is latest. The name is a required argument.

Examples:

  # Update all plugins to their latest available version
  steampipe plugin update --all

  # Update a common plugin (turbot/aws)
  steampipe plugin update aws

  # Hide progress bars during update
  steampipe plugin update --progress=false aws

Usage:
  steampipe plugin update [flags] [registry/org/]name[@version]

Flags:
      --all        Update all plugins to its latest available version
  -h, --help       Help for plugin update
      --progress   Display installation progress (default true)

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Execute SQL queries interactively, or by a query argument.

Open a interactive SQL query console to Steampipe to explore your data and run
multiple queries. If QUERY is passed on the command line then it will be run
immediately and the command will exit.

Examples:

  # Open an interactive query console
  steampipe query

  # Run a specific query directly
  steampipe query "select * from cloud"

Usage:
  steampipe query [flags]

Flags:
      --export strings               Export output to file, supported format: sps (snapshot)
      --header                       Include column headers csv and table output (default true)
  -h, --help                         Help for query
      --input                        Enable interactive prompts (default true)
      --output output                Output format; one of: snapshot, sps, table, csv, json, line (default table)
      --pipes-host string            Turbot Pipes host (default "pipes.turbot.com")
      --pipes-token string           Turbot Pipes authentication token
      --progress                     Display snapshot upload status (default true)
      --query-timeout int            The query timeout
      --search-path strings          Set a custom search_path for the steampipe user for a query session (comma-separated)
      --search-path-prefix strings   Set a prefix to the current search path for a query session (comma-separated)
      --separator string             Separator string for csv output (default ",")
      --share                        Create snapshot in Turbot Pipes with 'anyone_with_link' visibility
      --snapshot                     Create snapshot in Turbot Pipes with the default (workspace) visibility
      --snapshot-location string     The location to write snapshots - either a local file path or a Turbot Pipes workspace
      --snapshot-tag stringArray     Specify tags to set on the snapshot
      --snapshot-title string        The title to give a snapshot
      --timing timing[=on]           Display query timing; one of: off, on, verbose, true, false (default off)
      --workspace-database string    Turbot Pipes workspace database (default "local")

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Steampipe service management.

Run Steampipe as a local service, exposing it as a database endpoint for
connection from any Postgres compatible database client.

Usage:
  steampipe service [command]

Available Commands:
  restart     Restart Steampipe service
  start       Start Steampipe in service mode
  status      Status of the Steampipe service
  stop        Stop Steampipe service

Flags:
  -h, --help   Help for service

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Use "steampipe service [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Restart the Steampipe service.

Usage:
  steampipe service restart [flags]

Flags:
      --force   Forces the service to restart, releasing all open connections and ports
  -h, --help    Help for service restart

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Start the Steampipe service.

Run Steampipe as a local service, exposing it as a database endpoint for
connection from any Postgres compatible database client.

Usage:
  steampipe service start [flags]

Flags:
      --database-listen local      Accept connections from: local (an alias for `localhost` only), `network` (an alias for `*`), or a comma separated list of hosts and/or IP addresses (default "network")
      --database-password string   Set the database password for this session
      --database-port int          Database service port (default 9193)
      --foreground                 Run the service in the foreground
  -h, --help                       Help for service start
      --show-password              View database password for connecting from another machine

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Status of the Steampipe service.

Report current status of the Steampipe database service.

Usage:
  steampipe service status [flags]

Flags:
      --all             Bypasses the INSTALL_DIR and reports status of all running steampipe services
  -h, --help            Help for service status
      --show-password   View database password for connecting from another machine

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")

Stop the Steampipe service.

Usage:
  steampipe service stop [flags]

Flags:
      --force   Forces all services to shutdown, releasing all open connections and ports
  -h, --help    Help for service stop

Global Flags:
      --install-dir string   Path to the Config Directory (default "/home/ctk/.steampipe")
      --workspace string     The workspace profile to use (default "default")
